pages.extract: Abrolhos is an archipelago off the coast of Bahia, a state of Northeast Brazil.

pages.title: Jaú National Park
pages.extract: Jaú National Park is in the Brazilian state of Amazonas. It is a world heritage-site and preserves many fine examples of Amazonian fauna and flora.

pages.title: Monterrey
pages.description: capital of the State of Nuevo Leon, Mexico
pages.extract: Monterrey is the third largest city in Mexico and the capital of the state of Nuevo León. It is the commercial, industrial, educational, and transportation hub of northern Mexico, also third in economic importance after  Mexico City and Mexico State. Although it is historically an industrial and commercial city (in fact most foreign visitors come for business purposes), tourists will be surprised at the wealth of cultural and entertainment attractions that the city has to offer.

pages.title: Namche Bazaar
pages.extract: Namche Bazaar (3440 m) is the unofficial capital of the Khumbu region of Nepal,  and is a major stop-off point for trekkers and climbers heading for Mount Everest base camp.

pages.title: Ozarks (Arkansas)
pages.description: portion of a wider highland region named Ozarks in the central-southern United States
pages.extract: The Ozarks in  Arkansas are part of the Ozarks mountains, as well as being considered a region in north-central Arkansas and southern Missouri.

pages.title: Remoulins
pages.extract: Remoulins is a town in Languedoc-Roussillon in France, best known for Roman aqueduct the Pont du Gard.

pages.title: Santa Clara (Cuba)
pages.description: city in Villa Clara province, Cuba
pages.extract: Santa Clara is the capital city of the Cuban province of Villa Clara.

pages.title: Wick (Scotland)
pages.description: town and royal burgh in Caithness, Highland, Scotland, UK
pages.extract: Wick is a town in  Caithness in the far northeast of Scotland, with a population of 6870 in 2020. The name comes from Norse vik, meaning a bay. The town first grew up north of the river: in the 19th century the fishing port of Pulteney was established to the south, when herring shoals moved away from the Hebrides to the seas around here, and initially only a rickety footbridge connected the two settlements. Caithness Glass originated in Wick in 1961, though production has now moved to Crieff in Perthshire. Wick (along with Thurso) is a good base for exploring the rugged northern coast around John o' Groats, or as a stopover for the Orkney ferries.

pages.title: Ratnapura
pages.extract: Ratnapura (also transliterated as Rathnapura) is the capital city of Sabaragamuwa Province, located on the Kalu Ganga (Black River) in south-central Sri Lanka, some 101 km southeast of the country's capital, Colombo. Its name means 'City of Gems'.

pages.title: Bolsover
pages.extract: Bolsover is a small market town of about 12,000 people (2011) in Derbyshire. The district of Bolsover contains fourteen small towns.

pages.title: Cotahuasi Canyon
pages.extract: Cotahuasi Canyon is in Southern Sierra of Peru, near Arequipa.

pages.title: Daulatabad
pages.description: human settlement in Aurangabad District, Aurangabad Division, Maharashtra, India
pages.extract: Daulatabad (दौलताबाद Daulatābād), also known as Devagiri (देवगिरी Devgirī), is a town in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, close to Aurangabad.

pages.title: Bandingilo National Park
pages.extract: Bandingilo National Park (also spelled Badingilo National Park) is in the Equatoria region of South Sudan. It's listed as a  UNESCO World Heritage Site together with Boma National Park.

pages.title: Pacific Northwest Trail
pages.description: hiking trail in the western USA
pages.extract: The Pacific Northwest Trail (PNT) is a 1,200 mi (1,900 km) hiking trail in the Pacific Northwest of the United States. It runs from the Continental Divide in Glacier National Park, Montana, to the Pacific Ocean at Cape Alava in Olympic National Park, Washington state.

pages.title: Gyirong
pages.extract: Gyirong (also Kyirong; Chinese: 吉隆 Jílóng) is a town and county in Xigaze prefecture, at the border of Tibet and Nepal.
